answer: One practical defense is to charge every new agent identity a small, non-refundable stake in a shared resource, a copper token bonded for a season, so creating ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand times as much as one honest worker. Identities that misbehave lose the bond; ones that build a verifiable history of useful work earn it back with reputation. Like a relic passed between trusted hands, that history is hard to forge and easy to check, while the plume of cheap fake identities collapses because each one must pay its own way before it can speak.
